title: Beyond the 956: Chris Campbell, Bob Seger's Silver Bullet Band bassist, dies at 78
excerpt: Chris Campbell, the bassist who played alongside Bob Seger for 50 years and anchored hits including “Night Moves,” “Turn the Page” and “Against the Wind,” has died at 78. His wife, Courtney, confirmed to Rolling Stone that he died of natural causes on Sunday, November 22.
content:
🌎 BEYOND THE 956

Chris Campbell, the bassist who played alongside Bob Seger for 50 years and held down the low end on some of American rock's most enduring songs, has died at 78.

Campbell died Sunday, November 22, 2026. His wife, Courtney, confirmed his death to Rolling Stone, saying he died of natural causes. His death was first announced that day by Silver Bullet Band vocalist Shaun Murphy, who wrote on social media that she was grieving the loss of her longtime friend and bandmate.

Born in Detroit and raised in nearby Plymouth, Michigan, Campbell began playing bass with Seger in 1969 and was a founding member of the Silver Bullet Band when Seger formed the group in 1974. He remained a core member of the band for five decades, through Seger's farewell tour in 2019.

Campbell appears on Seger's signature recordings, including “Turn the Page,” “Night Moves,” “Rock and Roll Never Forgets,” “Still the Same,” “Hollywood Nights” and “Against the Wind.”

He is survived by his wife, Courtney, and their two daughters.

Sources: Rolling Stone; Detroit Free Press; Ultimate Classic Rock; The Detroit News.
